2027 Ford LMDh Hypercar Spotted at Monza, Coyote V8 Screams
10 photos
Photo: NM2255 | Raw Car Sounds/YouTube
Back in early 2025, Ford revealed that it plans to return to top-tier endurance racing with an LMDh race car. The hypercar is set to join the 2027 season of the FIA World Endurance Championship. The prototype has yet to get an official unveiling, but it's been spotted testing at the Monza circuit , in Italy.
The LMDh race car was first seen at the Paul Ricard circuit in France back in August. Ford also ran tests at the Portimão circuit in Portugal and at Silverstone. At Monza, the company began using a second chassis (though only one is captured in the video below).
Ford has yet to name its endurance racer, but we do know it's being developed in collaboration with Oreca, which provides the chassis. The vehicle features a naturally-aspirated 5.4-liter V8 engine derived from the Coyote. The mill was fitted onto the chassis and fired up for the first time in July 2026 . The hybrid system delivers 680 horsepower.
As seen in previous testing sessions, the car featured a blue-and-white camouflage-style design. Apart from a few details unique to this car (like the headlamps, for instance), Ford's LMDh racer looks very familiar. It has the typical canopy-style center section, a high center fin, a massive rear wing, and a heavily contoured front splitter and rear diffuser.
Ford's new hypercar will mark the company's return to top-tier endurance racing after several decades. Ford's last effort (that also included racing at Le Mans) dates all the way back to 1969. That's when the GT40 won the 24 Hours of Le Mans for the fourth consecutive year.
Ford has campaigned a race car based on the modern GT in recent years. A factory-backed effort joined the World Endurance Championship in the LM GTE-Pro, scoring a class win at the 2016 24 Hours of Le Mans.
Ford's yet-unnamed prototype is one of two LMDh race cars that will join the 2027 season. The other one is the McLaren MCL-HY. Unlike the Ford hypercar, the McLaren uses a chassis developed by Dallara.
The 2027 FIA WEC season will include nine events, with the 6 Hours of Silverstone returning to the calendar for the first time since 2019. The championship will commence in March in Qatar and will conclude in November in Bahrain. The 24 Hours of Le Mans race is scheduled on June 12-13.
The hypercar class will see no fewer than nine automakers battle for supremacy. Ford and McLaren will join Aston Martin, Toyota, Cadillac, BMW, Genesis, Ferrari, and Peugeot. Alpine will not return for the 2027 season.
Ford Racing will fully reveal its 2027 hypercar in late November. Until that happens, hit the play button below to see it doing quick laps around Monza. Make sure you crank up the volume to hear the Coyote V8 engine scream.
